article: 美しい数式5選：定理と式の正確な意味
scope: Compared the full Japanese article and twelve translations, including every formula, hypothesis, quantifier, mathematical term, localized Fermat link, description, and cited reference.
findings: Removed the duplicate future publication date and retained 2022-10-05 as publication date; set lastmod to 2026-11-24.
Stated Wilson’s theorem with its integer m>1 iff form and defined factorial notation.
Distinguished Euler’s general formula from the identity at x=pi, specifying radians and the real domain.
Clarified positive-integer and n>=3 conditions in Fermat’s Last Theorem.
Replaced an ambiguous ellipsis with the infinite Basel series notation.
Limited Euler’s polynomial prime claim to n=0..39 and added the counterexample n=40, where the value is 1681=41^2.
Added five mathematical/university references in all languages.

post/好きな数式/index.en.md.summary: Compared all mathematical statements and notation in the complete Japanese article and twelve translations with university and mathematical references; clarified hypotheses, radians, the infinite series, and the finite range of Euler’s polynomial.

meaning.note: Compared theorem statements, domains, quantifiers, equation exponents, and the n=0..39 range across the source and every translation; explicitly noted that n=40 gives a composite value.

terminology.note: Checked Wilson’s theorem, Euler’s formula versus identity, Fermat’s Last Theorem, Basel problem, prime/composite, factorial, radians, and the meanings of i and pi in every language.

mathematics.note: Verified Wilson’s congruence and iff form, Euler’s formula and x=pi identity, Fermat’s positive-integer statement for n>=3, the Basel sum, and Euler polynomial values for n=0..39 with counterexample 1681=41^2 at n=40.

code.note: The article contains no executable code or commands.

links.note: Checked five cited references from Wolfram MathWorld, Euler-Franeker Memorial University, University of Cambridge, University of Kentucky, and Cambridge University Press; retained the language-specific Fermat article links.

limitations: AI-assisted mathematical review; no human mathematician or native-speaker certification.
The formulas were checked against the cited references but no independent formal proof or computer algebra verification was performed.
